title: Action-Support Likelihood Audits Predict Rollout Consistency Failures in Text-Based World Models

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution frames and targets the world-to-real (W2R) transfer failure problem in text-based world models. This specific framing of W2R transfer failure under policy shift is not explicitly addressed in any prior paper. While several papers (e.g., [1], [12], [22]) discuss rollout consistency or model errors in reinforcement learning and world models, they do not explicitly target the W2R transfer problem or its implications under policy shift. Papers like [6], [8], and [15] address distribution shift broadly in offline RL but do not focus on the W2R transfer failure problem in text-based world models.

### Mechanism
The mechanism proposes a support-based diagnostic framework to measure how well rollout actions are supported by the training distribution. Papers such as [16] and [21] discuss policy constraints based on support sets of behavior policies, which is conceptually similar to the proposed mechanism. For example, [16] introduces "Supported Policy Optimization," which constrains policies to perform actions within the support set of the behavior policy. Similarly, [21] discusses "Policy Constraint by Only Support Constraint," which confines actions to the support set of the behavior policy. These approaches share the same underlying primitive of using support-based constraints to address distribution shift, even though the specific application to W2R transfer in text-based world models is new.

### Evaluation
The evaluation is positioned as a complementary problem to prior world-model work and motivated by offline RL out-of-distribution intuitions. This qualitative evaluation design does not introduce a new benchmark, metric, or protocol. Prior papers such as [6], [8], [15], and [16] use similar evaluation designs motivated by offline RL and distribution shift, including qualitative analyses and comparisons of rollout consistency or policy performance under distribution shift. The evaluation design is therefore covered.

### Domain
The domain is text-based (LLM) world models for planning and rollout verification. While prior papers like [1], [12], and [22] address world models and rollout verification, they focus on embodied navigation or robot action-conditioned models rather than text-based world models. However, the general application area of world models for planning and rollout verification is shared across these papers, making the domain covered.
